content.intro: Cursor is an AI-first code editor built on Visual Studio Code, featuring powerful code generation, intelligent suggestions, and multi-file editing capabilities. Explore the system prompts that power Cursor's AI features.

sections.heading: What is Cursor?
sections.content: Cursor is a revolutionary AI-powered code editor that combines the familiar interface of VS Code with advanced AI capabilities. It enables developers to write code faster through natural language instructions, automated code generation, and intelligent code understanding.

sections.heading: Key Features
sections.content: Cursor offers a comprehensive suite of AI-powered features designed to enhance developer productivity:
bullets: Multi-file editing with AI understanding of your entire codebase
Automatic bug fixing and code optimization

sections.heading: Understanding Cursor's System Prompts
sections.content: Cursor's AI capabilities are powered by sophisticated system prompts that guide the underlying language model. These prompts define how Cursor interprets your requests, generates code, and interacts with your codebase. Understanding these prompts can help you leverage Cursor more effectively.

faqs.question: What AI model does Cursor use?
faqs.answer: Cursor supports multiple AI models including GPT-4, Claude, and other leading language models. Users can choose their preferred model based on their needs and subscription tier.

faqs.question: Is Cursor free to use?
faqs.answer: Cursor offers a free tier with limited AI requests per month, plus paid Pro and Business tiers with more features and higher usage limits.

faqs.question: How does Cursor compare to GitHub Copilot?
faqs.answer: While both offer AI code assistance, Cursor provides a full IDE experience with features like multi-file editing and codebase understanding that go beyond simple code completion.

faqs.question: Is my code private when using Cursor?
faqs.answer: Cursor offers privacy modes and local-first options. You can configure which code is sent to AI models and choose enterprise-grade security options for sensitive projects.
